new_entities.name: Leaky-gut zonulin supplements
new_entities.description: Probiotic, synbiotic, and other supplement formulations marketed to lower zonulin or repair a presumed 'leaky gut' state.

edges.effect_quant: A 2020 meta-analysis of nine trials with 496 intervention and 443 control participants reported lower serum zonulin after probiotic or synbiotic supplementation, but heterogeneity was extreme (I² 97.8%). A 2024 systematic review in healthy people found only limited moderate-quality support for probiotics or chicory inulin and concluded there was still no strong evidence that diet-based interventions reliably alter intestinal barrier permeability.
edges.population: adults given supplements or diet-linked products marketed for lowering zonulin or improving presumed intestinal barrier dysfunction
edges.mechanism: Some supplements may shift microbiota composition or tight-junction signaling, but the clinical meaning of serum zonulin changes remains uncertain and the 'leaky gut' label often overstates what those biomarkers prove.
edges.summary: This is a mixed, low-certainty claim-check edge. Some supplement trials move zonulin or related permeability markers in favorable directions, but the biomarker field is noisy and does not justify strong consumer-facing claims that these products reliably 'heal leaky gut'.
edges.caveats: Lower zonulin is not the same thing as proving symptom benefit or reversing a validated disease mechanism. Many marketed products extrapolate far beyond the underlying human evidence.

evidence.citation: Karbalaei M et al 2020 Iran J Public Health
